claim_scope.topic: HSConfig source-claim quality classification for pre-run package generation.
claim_scope.boundary: Verify how HSConfig should classify source-backed static semantics, guide-backed mulligan claims, runtime-evidence-only numeric tuning, low-confidence claims, and unsupported claims without ever turning semantic weakness into a deck-generation blocker.

verified_classes.classification: Treat as pre-run usable semantics when the claim is explicitly static-semantics-backed or when static card metadata proves a safe semantic family such as start-of-game hero power transform.
verified_classes.repo_behavior: This class may support runtime lowering only through documented surfaces and only when the claim kind is runtime-lowerable.

verified_classes.classification: Treat as the strongest normal Step 1 mulligan input when the claim kind is an exact mulligan keep or discard claim and the selector and condition are supported.
verified_classes.repo_behavior: This class lowers into Mulligan.json unless the keep would incorrectly represent a non-hand start-of-game effect.

verified_classes.classification: Treat as report-visible but Step 1 write-blocked tuning.
verified_classes.repo_behavior: This class is carried in GlobalValues authority warnings and blocked-until-runtime-evidence rows rather than emitted as Step 1 numeric overlays.

verified_classes.classification: Treat as review-only source depth debt.
verified_classes.repo_behavior: This class stays visible in coverage, warnings, and gap reports but must not lower into runtime config.

verified_classes.classification: Treat as explicit suppression, not silent fallback.
verified_classes.repo_behavior: This class records a concrete suppression reason and remains non-blocking unless the package becomes technically invalid for separate reasons.

claim_scope.no_block_boundary: HSConfig must keep `technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE` and `runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply` separate from semantic strength labels such as `SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG` or `VALID_BUT_NOT_GUIDE_STRONG`.

runtime_surfaces: CardID.json when the claim kind maps to a documented card-behavior surface such as `hero_power_transform`.
GlobalValues.json posture overlays only when the input is `gameplan_posture`, not raw numeric tuning.
runtime_surface_implication.notes: Static semantics can also remain purely classificatory in research and confidence summaries when no documented runtime row exists.
Requires exact mulligan claim kind, supported selector, supported condition, and no start-of-game non-hand effect misuse.
Baseline GlobalValues plus source-backed posture overlays may still emit; runtime-only numeric tuning may not.
These claims stay in claim coverage, closure routing, and warning summaries.
Suppression is explicit per surface, for example `claim_kind_not_cardid_surface`, `unsupported_condition`, or `unsupported_mechanic_runtime_block`.

safe_to_emit_step1.overall_rule: Yes for runtime-lowerable guide-backed or static-semantics-backed claims; no for runtime-evidence-only numeric tuning, low-confidence claims, and unsupported claims.

by_claim_class.reason: `claim_readiness=source_backed_static_semantics` is runtime-lowerable when the claim kind is supported and the runtime row is documented.
Exact guide-backed mulligan claims are the normal Step 1 authority for Mulligan.json.
The gate explicitly returns `requires_runtime_evidence` and the authority matrix records the row under `blocked_until_runtime_evidence`.
Report-only readiness labels and report-only trust ceilings are not runtime-lowerable.
Unsupported claim kinds, unsupported conditions, or unsupported runtime blocks must be suppressed instead of guessed.

safe_to_emit_step1.deck_generation_impact: Unsafe claim classes must not block base deck generation; they only reduce semantic strength and add warnings or gap reports.

blocked_or_report_only_cases.case: GlobalValues numeric tuning that requires live runtime evidence
blocked_or_report_only_cases.visibility_surface: GlobalValues authority matrix and operator warnings
coverage status, warnings, and source-claim-gap follow-up
blocked_or_report_only_cases.why: Low-confidence and contract-gap labels are explicitly outside the runtime-lowerable readiness set.
The trust ceiling is an explicit ban on runtime lowering.

blocked_or_report_only_cases.case: Mulligan keep claims for start-of-game non-hand effects such as hero power transforms
blocked_or_report_only_cases.visibility_surface: mulligan suppressed rules plus CardID effect rows when separately supported
blocked_or_report_only_cases.why: The repo suppresses the opening-hand keep because the effect does not require drawing the card.

blocked_or_report_only_cases.why: HSConfig must preserve provenance and explicit reasons instead of inventing JSON.

blocked_or_report_only_cases.visibility_surface: card behavior option-resolution and suppression outputs
blocked_or_report_only_cases.why: Resolved identity may lower later, but unresolved identity must not be guessed.

autonomy_risk.risk: A start-of-game enabler can be misclassified as an opening-hand keep.
autonomy_risk.failure_mode: Generic wording like `keep` creates a fake mulligan anchor.
autonomy_risk.control: Require exact `claim_kind=mulligan_keep` and suppress non-hand start-of-game effects from Mulligan.json.

autonomy_risk.risk: Deck-only generation can over-promote generic or adjacent guide advice.
autonomy_risk.failure_mode: A package looks strong even though a key mulligan or combo claim is only weakly sourced.
autonomy_risk.control: Keep low-confidence rows visible, maintain first-missing-chain routing, and refuse `SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG` when guide gaps remain.

autonomy_risk.risk: Runtime-only numeric tuning leaks into Step 1.
autonomy_risk.failure_mode: GlobalValues numbers are emitted as if they were source-backed posture decisions.
autonomy_risk.control: Keep raw numeric tuning in `blocked_until_runtime_evidence`; only posture overlays may change Step 1 GlobalValues.

autonomy_risk.risk: Unsupported conditions or mechanics are silently converted into guessed runtime rows.
autonomy_risk.failure_mode: The package becomes semantically dishonest or technically unsafe.
autonomy_risk.control: Emit explicit suppression reasons and preserve the no-block promise only for technically valid packages.

autonomy_risk.risk: Operators confuse semantic weakness with runtime apply authority.
autonomy_risk.failure_mode: Valid packages are wrongly blocked because they are not guide-strong.
autonomy_risk.control: Keep `VALID_PACKAGE` and `load_safe_apply` as the runtime gate and treat semantic debt as warnings.

recommended_contract_rule.overall_rule: Classify every claim twice: first by semantic quality, then by runtime-lowering authority. Only technically invalid packages may block generation or apply. Everything else must either lower through a documented surface or stay visible as a warning, suppression, or gap report.

classification_rules.lowering_rule: Allow Step 1 lowering only when the claim kind is one of the supported runtime surfaces and the row can be represented with documented syntax.
classification_rules.status_effect: Can contribute to `STATIC_SEMANTICS_USABLE`; can also participate in stronger statuses if all other gaps are closed.

classification_rules.lowering_rule: Lower to Mulligan.json only from explicit mulligan keep or discard claim kinds with supported selectors and conditions.
classification_rules.status_effect: Helps satisfy mulligan coverage needed for `SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG`.

classification_rules.lowering_rule: Never lower directly in Step 1; record the key and reason under `blocked_until_runtime_evidence`.
classification_rules.status_effect: Adds warnings but must not block a technically valid package.

classification_rules.lowering_rule: Do not lower to runtime config; retain as review-only evidence and closure work.
classification_rules.status_effect: Prevents `SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG`, often yields `VALID_BUT_NOT_GUIDE_STRONG`, but does not block deck generation.

classification_rules.lowering_rule: Suppress with a concrete surface-specific reason; never emit guessed runtime JSON.
classification_rules.status_effect: May add semantic blockers for strongness, but remains non-blocking for the base package unless technical validation fails.

recommended_contract_rule.operator_meaning: The durable product meaning is: every valid deck gets a load-safe initial package; not every valid deck is guide-strong, fully lowered, or runtime-tuned.
